evals.prompt: Design the edge states for a data table page that shows spider task results. The table has columns for name, status, and created date. There's a search bar and pagination.
evals.expected_output: Documents all 6 states: empty (no results — invitation to create), loading (skeleton for table shape), error (API failure with retry), boundary (max page, zero results for search term), permission (viewer can see but not create), offline (cached last results or network error). Does NOT only document the happy path.
expectations: Documents all 6 states (empty/loading/error/boundary/permission/offline)
Empty state includes a call to action, not just 'no data'
Permission state addressed (what does an unauthorized user see?)
Offline state addressed (at least as a network error message)

evals.prompt: Create the design tokens for a new admin dashboard. Brand color is teal (#0D9488).
evals.expected_output: Produces a three-layer token file (primitive → semantic → component) covering ALL token categories — color, spacing scale, typography (size+weight+line-height sets), radius, shadows named by purpose, motion duration+easing, breakpoints. Semantic color names (color-primary), with a full set per semantic color (hover/subtle/text-on-subtle). Does NOT deliver a palette of hex values and call it tokens.
expectations: Defines tokens beyond color: spacing, typography, radius, shadow, motion, breakpoints all present
Uses semantic naming (color-primary) not color names (color-teal) for the consumption layer
Each semantic color comes as a set (base/hover/subtle/text-on-subtle)
Typography tokens bundle size+weight+line-height together
Breakpoints are defined as tokens

evals.prompt: Design the visual direction for the marketing landing page of our skills marketplace.
evals.expected_output: First grounds in subject matter (what a skills marketplace is, who visits, what the page's primary job is), then produces a plan: 4-6 named hex colors, typeface roles, a one-line layout concept, and principles. Critiques the plan against the recognizable AI defaults (cream+serif+terracotta, dark+acid-green, SaaS card kit, ALL-CAPS eyebrows, arrow-suffixed links) and revises anything that matches. Spends boldness in one memorable element.
expectations: States the subject matter/audience/page-job before any visual choices
Produces a plan (palette, type, layout, principles) before implementation details
Explicitly checks the plan against AI-default clusters and revises matches
Does NOT deliver cream #F4F1EA + serif + terracotta #D97757, or near-black + acid green, without brief-driven justification
Concentrates visual boldness in one element rather than decorating everywhere

evals.prompt: Write the UI copy for the LLM provider connection test feature: the button, and the copy for empty (no provider configured yet), testing, success, and failure states.
evals.expected_output: Button says what happens ('测试连接'). Failure copy states what happened + what to do now ('API Key 无效，检查后重新测试'), no apology, no vagueness. Empty state is an invitation to act, not '暂无数据'. Success toast keeps the action's name ('连接成功' after '测试连接'). All copy is active voice, user-perspective.
expectations: Button label states the consequence ('测试连接'), not a vague verb ('提交'/'执行'/'确定')
Error copy contains both what happened and what to do next; no '抱歉' and no '出了点问题' style vagueness
Empty state invites action instead of a dead-end '暂无数据'
Success message keeps the trigger action's vocabulary (test → 连接成功, not '操作完成')

evals.prompt: We're adding four FRs to the admin console: user CRUD, role assignment, department tree management, audit log viewer. Design the information architecture for them.
evals.expected_output: Maps each FR to a screen and a menu location, reuses existing pages where they exist (users list already has CRUD — role assignment extends it rather than duplicating), introduces new screens only for genuinely new capabilities (audit viewer), states the navigation group each screen belongs to, and flags which FRs need a flow document (role assignment with permission matrix) versus simple CRUD.
expectations: Every FR maps to exactly one primary screen location — no FR orphaned, no invented screens for non-FRs
Reuses the existing user management page instead of creating a duplicate CRUD screen
Assigns each screen to a navigation group
Identifies which FR needs a flow document (role assignment / permission matrix) versus plain CRUD
Does NOT place audit log viewer inside user management (cross-cutting data belongs in its own section)

evals.prompt: task: explore. Feature: first-run experience of a personal finance app — after linking a bank account, the user should understand where their money went last month. Brand character: calm, trustworthy, a little warm. Produce the design directions deliverable.
evals.expected_output: Studies references and states what to take/avoid. Produces credible structurally different options for unresolved choices (e.g. story-style month recap, category treemap dashboard, conversational Q&A) as rendered HTML prototypes with screenshots at supported target sizes. Each direction names a signature moment tied to the Aha (e.g. the month's biggest surprise revealed with a gentle count-up), its trade-offs, risks, build cost and an AI-default self-check. Ends with a reasoned recommendation and leaves the pick to the human.
expectations: Presents credible distinct options suited to the unresolved design decision without a fixed count quota
Each direction names a signature moment
References screenshots or rendered prototypes
Gives a recommendation

rubric.criterion: Directions differ in structure or interaction model, not just colour
Directions are rendered artifacts that were looked at (screenshots/prototypes), not only prose
Each direction has a concrete signature moment tied to the Aha
Directions express the stated brand character and avoid unjustified AI-default looks
Recommendation is reasoned with trade-offs and leaves the choice to the human

evals.prompt: task: design-qa. The picked direction D2 shows the monthly recap with a count-up animation on the total and a highlighted 'biggest surprise' card. Build screenshots: the total appears instantly without animation, the surprise card uses the default grey card style, the empty state (no transactions) shows '暂无数据', and focus outlines were removed. Write accept-design.md.
evals.expected_output: Compare supplied build images to the approved final design; identify focus accessibility and state/experience deviations. Check reduced-motion context before treating absent animation as a defect. Label screenshot-only limits, rank by user impact and route actual mismatches without claiming live execution.
expectations: Identifies the missing signature moment
Flags the removed focus outline as an accessibility problem
Rejects '暂无数据' as the empty state copy
Ends with a verdict line '结论：'

rubric.criterion: Assesses the approved experience and reduced-motion behavior, without assuming animation loss outranks an accessibility defect.
Correct severity ranking incl. accessibility floor

evals.prompt: An existing desktop-only admin table needs an approved permission-denied state. Same layout/components/tokens; no brand change. Produce final handoff and design QA plan.
evals.expected_output: Use reuse mode and cite existing authorization; no mandatory three directions, web quota or mobile layout. Provide runnable final state source, component IDs and canonical token/version references; map frontend integration and compare real build at supported viewport. Do not treat prototype capture as implementation evidence.
expectations: Addresses the supplied task and its evidence/authority limits

rubric.criterion: Use reuse mode and cite existing authorization; no mandatory three directions, web quota or mobile layout. Provide runnable final state source, component IDs and canonical token/version references; map frontend integration and compare real build at supported viewport. Do not treat prototype capture as implementation evidence.
